Bind a model specification to prepared inputs

Source: R/08-spax_bind.R
dot-bind_spax_spec.Rd

The private step inside spax() that turns a data-free spax_spec (see spec_clm()) and checked ae_prepared_inputs into the existing ae_problem, built through clm_allocation(). It checks the demand groups, translates the specification into the arguments of clm_allocation(), decides whether the model is fitted or evaluated and refuses a decay that is undefined at a zero travel time.

Usage

.bind_spax_spec(spec, data)

Arguments

spec

A spax_spec from spec_clm() or spec_huff().

data

An ae_prepared_inputs, from prep_data().

Value

A list: problem (the ae_problem), mode ("fit" or "evaluate"), theta_given (NULL in fit mode; in evaluate mode the named values of the free parameters, in the order of problem$theta$names) and held, a named numeric vector of the values that are neither fitted nor given: held sigma or sigma.<group> (fit mode only, since in evaluate mode sigma is in theta_given), v0 or v0.<group> (v0 = 0 for the Huff model), beta when it is a number and kappa.

Details

Mode. The mode is "fit" when any parameter is free ("fit" in its slot) and "evaluate" when every parameter has a value. In fit mode the held values of a model with demand groups go through fixed; an ungrouped model cannot hold its sigma while something else is fitted. In evaluate mode sigma is bound as a free parameter and its value is returned as theta_given, for evaluate_allocation(); nothing goes into fixed.
